loop.target: refine, clean, improve and test the commissar feature until fully release ready
recentTexts:
**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.

**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

loop.target: refine, clean, improve and test the commissar feature until fully release ready
recentTexts:
**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.

recentTexts:
**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.

loop.target: refine, clean, improve and test the commissar feature until fully release ready
recentTexts:
**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.

loop.target: refine, clean, improve and test the commissar feature until fully release ready
recentTexts:
**Iteration 10 shipped** (`ffaba04`, pushed): two reviewer-facing cleanups —

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.
